frase_inicial: Timothy and Melanie: let's go step by step—one small, useful thing to start.

tarjetas.frente: The high‑rate card is costing you both energy.
tarjetas.reverso: Carrying that balance quietly eats your money each month and holds your score back. Paying part of it from cash frees you to protect the family next.
tarjetas.detalle: Pay $6,800 from cash toward the 18% credit card to reduce high‑rate revolving exposure and clear the gate.

tarjetas.frente: Life cover is one thing Liam and Josh depend on.
tarjetas.reverso: Your current policies leave a big gap if one of you dies. Adding more life cover protects the kids and makes other plans feel safer.
tarjetas.detalle: Add $235,000 of life insurance to raise total household cover toward recommended levels for two earners with young children.

tarjetas.frente: You have spare cash that can work for you.
tarjetas.reverso: You hold a cushion well above the emergency target. Using a slice of the extra cash now can pay the costly card or start protection without hurting your safety buffer.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash today: $150,800; cash above reserve and near‑term goals: $60,222.50.

tarjetas.frente: No umbrella policy leaves home and savings exposed.
tarjetas.reverso: Home and car insurance don't cover big liability claims. A modest umbrella policy would shield the family’s savings and give peace of mind.
tarjetas.detalle: Recommended umbrella: $1,000,000; currently no umbrella in place.

tarjetas.frente: College saving can start slowly and still help.
tarjetas.reverso: Nothing is set aside yet for Liam and Josh. Small regular contributions will build over years so college won’t surprise you later.
tarjetas.detalle: Extra yearly saving needed for education (first year): $4,609.22 for both children combined.
